population.span: In a randomized, open-label, event-driven, noninferiority trial involving 4832 patients who had acute symptomatic pulmonary embolism with or without deep-vein thrombosis

endpoint.span: The principal safety outcome was major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding.

estimate.span: The principal safety outcome occurred in 10.3% of patients in the rivaroxaban group and 11.4% of those in the standard-therapy group (hazard ratio, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.76 to 1.07; P=0.23).

analysis_set.span: impairment of activities of daily life. | TIME FRAME: 3-, 6- or 12-month study treatment period | POPULATION: The valid-for-safety analysis population consisted of all participants who were randomized with valid informed consent and received at least one dose of anticoagulant study treatment after randomization

treatment_strategy.span: we compared rivaroxaban (15 mg twice daily for 3 weeks, followed by 20 mg once daily) with standard therapy with enoxaparin followed by an adjusted-dose vitamin K antagonist for 3, 6, or 12 months

follow_up.span: Percentage of Participants With Clinically Relevant Bleeding, Treatment-emergent (Time Window: Until 2 Days After Last Dose)

candidate_rejections.span: Major bleeding was observed in 26 patients (1.1%) in the rivaroxaban group and 52 patients (2.2%) in the standard-therapy group (hazard ratio, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.31 to 0.79; P=0.003).
candidate_rejections.why: Major bleeding alone, a component of the served composite endpoint.

entry_population_matches_question.why: Acute symptomatic PE with or without DVT is a subset of acute symptomatic VTE; comparator is enoxaparin followed by a VKA.
entry_population_matches_question.span: 4832 patients who had acute symptomatic pulmonary embolism with or without deep-vein thrombosis

notes: EINSTEIN-PE (NCT00439777). Served row 0.90 (0.76-1.07) matches the principal safety outcome HR, which the abstract defines as major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding. Registry Outcome 5 ('Clinically Relevant Bleeding' = major + clinically relevant non-major) reproduces 10.3% vs 11.4% and HR 0.90 (95% CI 0.76 to 1.07) in the valid-for-safety population (2412 vs 2405), which is why the analysis_set and follow_up (treatment-emergent, until 2 days after last dose, within the 3-, 6- or 12-month treatment period) are bound from the registry. Only percentages, not event counts, are printed in the estimate span.
